svg.title: Anubis Lindnor ransomware intrusion kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: initial access not determined; Lindnor backdoor on two Microsoft SQL Servers; about 13 executables and 5 vulnerable drivers dropped within an hour; kernel callback removal, AnyDesk registered for Safe Mode with Networking and a new local user; Anubis payload iservice.exe blocked before encryption; response and break points. Detection anchors are the SafeBoot Network AnyDesk registry key, the published hashes and file names, driver drops and the two C2 hosts.
svg.text: Anubis (Hawkmoth RaaS): Lindnor backdoor, BYOVD killers and Safe Mode AnyDesk
Vendor: Symantec (2026-11-05) | Date: 2026-11-10 | Cluster: Hawkmoth / Anubis (medium) | Day 140
U.S. ORGANIZATION, OCTOBER 2026
Initial access not determined; the first indicator is a new backdoor on two MSSQL servers [unknown]
Symantec: "We did not identify how the attackers gained initial access"; Lindnor sat on the only two Microsoft SQL Servers affected
No xp_cmdshell, credential or lateral-movement detail is published; the SQL abuse path is a hunting hypothesis, not a fact
Lindnor was also seen on two unrelated networks where no ransomware followed
Initial access: unknown MSSQL x2
Backdoor.Lindnor runs as a service on both SQL servers [T1543.003 T1036.005 T1071.001]
healthcontroller64.exe in a folder imitating a Chrome component directory; svchelper.exe in a VMware folder
Beacons process ID, Windows version, own path, computer, user, domain and logon server; primary and fallback C2, both port 443
Two other hashes: powerhost.exe / eventwatcher.exe and volumeproxy.exe (same family)
msrcontrib[.]com cfgsync-relay.eastus.cloudapp.azure[.]com
About an hour later: at least 13 executables and 5 publicly known vulnerable drivers are dropped [T1068 T1562.001]
gbbsym.exe and symgooq.exe masquerade as Symantec; -l lists kernel callbacks through a loaded driver, -d lists and removes them
huntreagent.exe and s1.exe (same size, different hashes) were not blocked; the other dropped executables were
Drivers: havoc.sys, monprocessex.sys, xhunter1.sys, bdapiutil64.sys, fly.sys; 11 of the 13 executables were new
gbbsym.exe -d symgooq.exe -d huntreagent.exe s1.exe
Safe Mode access: AnyDesk installed, local user added, safemode.exe registers the service [T1219 T1136.001 T1562.009]
Genuine AnyDesk is installed, a new local user is added to a local group (names not published), then safemode.exe runs
Registry write: HKLM SYSTEM CurrentControlSet Control SafeBoot Network AnyDesk = Service, so AnyDesk survives Safe Mode with Networking
Rationale in the report: security tools usually do not fully run in Safe Mode, leaving a window to use the drivers
reg.exe add ...\SafeBoot\Network\AnyDesk /ve /t REG_SZ /d Service /f
Anubis payload iservice.exe: blocked before execution; no files encrypted [T1486]
Appends .anubis, drops restore files.txt and restore files.html, claims data theft; optional wiper mode empties file contents
Hawkmoth runs Anubis as RaaS (Sphinx rebrand, Dec 2024); about 96 victims claimed in 12 months, 52 percent in the U.S.
A July 2026 Anubis case used Megasync, WinSCP, Filezilla and S3browser for exfiltration (context, not this intrusion)
iservice.exe *.anubis restore files.txt
Response and break points [no technique]
Alert on SafeBoot Network service keys not in the baseline; hunt the published hashes and the two C2 hosts; review SQL Server hosts first
Enable the vulnerable driver blocklist / HVCI, tamper protection and Safe Mode boot auditing; remove unapproved remote-access tools
Initial access is unknown: treat the SQL servers as the investigation start and re-validate every indicator before blocking
SafeBoot\Network | BYOVD blocklist | SQL host review
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 rules), Suricata sids 9980001-9980003, PEAK H1-H3. Derived from the Symantec report as relayed; no sample analysis.
Break points: SafeBoot Network key alert, hash and name sweep, C2 DNS/SNI block, driver blocklist. Initial access and SQL abuse method unpublished.
